## Install

In the Quarto project that holds your lessons, run:

```bash
quarto add ryjohnson09/quarto-simulator
```

This copies the extension into `_extensions/quarto-simulator/`. Commit that
folder with your lessons. Lessons can be rendered with Quarto 1.9 or later.
The renderer inside the playground is Quarto 1.10.19, whichever version
renders the lesson.

To update the extension later, run the same command again.

## Set up a lesson

Add the filter to the lesson's YAML, and set `engine: markdown`:

```yaml
---
title: "My lesson"
engine: markdown
filters:
  - quarto-simulator
---
```

`engine: markdown` matters. Without it, Quarto sees the ```` ```{r} ```` and
```` ```{python} ```` cells inside your playgrounds and runs them with knitr or
Jupyter while rendering the lesson, before the playground ever sees them. If the
lesson itself must run code, see [Starter documents in files](#starter-documents-in-files).

The lesson must be served over HTTP, as `quarto preview`, GitHub Pages or any
web server does. Opening the HTML file directly from disk won't work.

## Your first playground

A playground is a `quarto-simulator` block whose content is the learner's
starting document. Use a fence with **more backticks than any fence inside
the document**. Four is enough when the document has ordinary code cells:

`````markdown
````{quarto-simulator}
---
title: "Hello"
---

## Introduction

Write *anything* here.

```{r}
1 + 1
```
````
`````

That block becomes:

````{quarto-simulator}
---
title: "Hello"
---

## Introduction

Write *anything* here.

```{r}
1 + 1
```
````

The first render downloads pandoc (about 16 MB) and, because this document
has an R cell, webR. Later renders take about half a second. Every playground
on the page shares the same pandoc and R.

### What learners can do

- **▶ Render**, or <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> +
  <kbd>K</kbd> as in RStudio and Positron (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> +
  <kbd>Enter</kbd> also works).
- **↺ Reset** to go back to the starting document.
- Read warnings and errors under the editor: YAML errors point to the line,
  unknown options get "did you mean" suggestions, and failed cells say which
  cell failed.

Edits are saved in the browser's `localStorage`, per page and per
playground, so they survive a reload.

## Playground options

Options go in `#|` lines at the top of the block, before the document:

| Option       | Default        | Meaning                                                                     |
|--------------|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `exercise`   | none           | ID that links the playground to checks, hints and solutions. See [Exercises](exercises.qmd) |
| `file`       | none           | Load the starting document from a file, relative to the lesson               |
| `height`     | `460`          | Height of the editor and preview, in pixels                                 |
| `layout`     | `horizontal`   | `vertical` stacks the preview under the editor                              |
| `column`     | body           | A Quarto column, such as `page-inset-right` or `page`                       |
| `autorender` | `true`         | Render when the playground first scrolls into view                          |
| `live`       | `false`        | Re-render as the learner types                                              |
| `filename`   | `document.qmd` | Name shown above the editor                                                 |

### Layout and size

A vertical layout suits narrow pages and long previews:

`````markdown
````{quarto-simulator}
#| layout: vertical
#| height: 260
#| filename: notes.qmd
---
title: "Stacked"
---

The preview is below the editor.
````
`````

````{quarto-simulator}
#| layout: vertical
#| height: 260
#| filename: notes.qmd
---
title: "Stacked"
---

The preview is below the editor.
````

### Live preview

With `live: true`, the preview updates shortly after the learner stops
typing. It suits short markdown-only documents; with code cells, every pause
re-runs the code.

`````markdown
````{quarto-simulator}
#| live: true
#| height: 220
Type here: **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, H~2~O, E = mc^2^.
````
`````

````{quarto-simulator}
#| live: true
#| height: 220
Type here: **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, H~2~O, E = mc^2^.
````

### Render on request

`autorender: false` waits for the learner to press **▶ Render**. Use it for
playgrounds that download large packages, so scrolling past them costs
nothing.

`````markdown
````{quarto-simulator}
#| autorender: false
#| height: 200
---
title: "Not rendered yet"
---

Press Render to see this document.
````
`````

````{quarto-simulator}
#| autorender: false
#| height: 200
---
title: "Not rendered yet"
---

Press Render to see this document.
````

## Starter documents in files {#starter-documents-in-files}

`#| file:` loads the starting document from a file, relative to the lesson.
The block is then empty apart from its options:

`````markdown
````{quarto-simulator}
#| file: _starters/report.qmd
````
`````

````{quarto-simulator}
#| file: _starters/report.qmd
````

Start the file name with `_` (or keep it in a folder whose name does) so that
a Quarto project doesn't render it as a page. Files also keep long starting
documents out of the lesson's source, and they are the way to use playgrounds
in a lesson that runs code itself: the lesson then has no nested cells, so it
doesn't need `engine: markdown`.

## Page settings

A `quarto-simulator` key in the lesson's YAML sets defaults for the page:

```yaml
quarto-simulator:
  column: page-inset-right   # default column for every playground
  pandoc-wasm-url: /assets/pandoc.wasm
  webr-url: https://webr.r-wasm.org/v0.6.0/webr.mjs
  pyodide-url: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v314.0.7/full/pyodide.mjs
```

The URLs say where pandoc, webR and Pyodide are downloaded from. The
defaults are public CDNs; see [hosting the binaries](how-it-works.qmd#hosting-and-embedding)
to serve them yourself.
